entities.summary:
Ovidius, also Saint Auditus, was the third Bishop of Braga; he is a Portuguese saint. Recognized as a religious figures from Sicily (50 CE, Sicily–135 CE). Ovidius played a crucial role in shaping the spiritual communities of the Roman Empire, particularly in the region of Portugal. His legacy as a bishop and saint has endured for centuries, influencing the development of Christian doctrine and practice in the Iberian Peninsula.

As a member of the Roman Catholic Church, Ovidius was deeply involved in the missionary work of Saint Patrick, who spread Christianity to the British Isles in the 5th century. Ovidius's own missionary efforts took him to the Iberian Peninsula, where he established a network of churches and monasteries that would later become the foundation of Portuguese Catholicism.

Ovidius's contributions to the Christian faith extend beyond his missionary work, as he also played a key role in the development of Christian doctrine and practice in the region. His teachings on the importance of prayer, fasting, and charity helped shape the spiritual practices of the early Christian community in Portugal.

Despite the passing of centuries, Ovidius's legacy continues to be felt in Portugal today. His feast day, celebrated on October 15th, is still observed with great devotion by the Portuguese Catholic Church.

A striking example of Ovidius's enduring impact is the Basilica of São Marcos in Braga, Portugal, which was built during his lifetime and features an impressive collection of Roman mosaics and artifacts.

Ovidius's story is a testament to the power of faith and determination, as he dedicated his life to spreading the teachings of Christianity to the people of Portugal. His legacy serves as a reminder of the importance of perseverance and devotion in the pursuit of spiritual growth and understanding.

In the words of Saint Ovidius himself, 'The Lord is my shepherd, I shall not want.' (Psalm 23:1)
